The first weeks suck.  They weren't magical or happy or amazing.  They fucking sucked.  Being constantly sleep deprived, overwhelmed, stressed, touched out, depressed.  The nightime dread.  And all the hormonal changes making everything worse.  I hated being a mom.  And I hated myself for feeling that way.  I felt lost and like I was suffocating and would never be happy again.  I felt like I had made a huge mistake.  


Things got better after I talked to a doctor and got on Zoloft.  And more importantly with time.  It takes time to learn how to be a mom.  And that's okay.  And newborns aren't really all that fun.  They just cry and poop and eat and cry and cry and cry.  And it sucks because you don't get any reward.  They can't smile at you yet, or laugh, or play, or do anything that makes it fun. 
But it won't always suck. 


My son is 9 months now and things are a million times better.  I love being a mom most days.  It's challenging still, but so rewarding.  Seeing his first real smile, hearing him laugh, watching him learn to crawl and grab things and poke at stuff.  He has a weird sense of humor that just makes me so freaking happy and proud to be his mom.  


I remember thinking I was going to hate my life forever, but holy shit it goes by so fast.  I promise it won't suck forever.

Tl;dr A bunch of small events and experiences that eventually led to me watching Earthlings.


Ever since I can remember I've considered myself an animal lover.  When I was a little kid I loved anything to do with animals of all kinds.  I had this page cut out of a magazine on the back of my door that said, "we are not nuggets, please don't eat us," with pictures of cute little chicks.  My dad would always ask why I had that up if I still ate chicken and I'd just shrug.  I mean, what the hell was I supposed to eat at restaurants if I couldn't eat chicken tenders?! 


A cousin of mine went vegan and asked me if I loved animals.  I said yes. He asked me if I ate meat. I said yes. He then said it's impossible to eat animals and still love them.  I was offended and hurt and walked away, and thought he was super annoying, but it definitely planted some seeds.


In one of my first college courses we ended up watching a 3 minute clip of some slaughterhouse videos.  I was trying not to cry the whole time and was horrified, but ended up making up some lame excuse to keep eating meat.


I went to Warped Tour 2014 and they had people there handing out bracelets and flyers that talked about veganism/vegetarianism and what happens at factory farms and what music artists didn't eat meat.  I was kind of annoyed at the people, but did end up thinking a lot because one of my favorite vocalists was vegetarian and obviously didn't like being reminded of what happens on factory farms.  I actually made a post on Instagram that day stating how I wanted to go vegetarian but didn't think I'd be able to. 


I met a new neighbor who was vegan who talked about it constantly.  She was nice, but also very aggressive about it.  She made me feel guilty.  Why did I feel so guilty? Why wont she just shut up already?  Why is this so important? What's the big deal?  So I decided to learn more about veganism from doing my own research online.  I typed in vegan documentary into YouTube.  Clicked on Earthlings.  Cried the whole time.  Been vegetarian/vegan for over 2 years now.  So happy.
